identity.title: Deliriogenic medication review: anticholinergics, benzodiazepines, opioids, new/changed drugs, thiazides

technique.how: Reconcile every drug against the MAR, pharmacy fill history and family/carer report, including OTC, herbal and PRN doses. Flag anticholinergics (antihistamines, TCAs, bladder antispasmodics), benzodiazepines/Z-drugs, opioids, dihydropyridines, steroids, and any drug started, stopped or dose-changed in the 72 h before the mental-status change; note thiazides/SSRIs as hyponatremia sources.
technique.prerequisites: Access to MAR/dispensing record and a collateral historian; the patient's own account is unreliable once delirious.

interpretation.positive_finding: One or more high-risk agents, or >3 medications added during admission, temporally preceding the confusion. Supports medication-induced delirium as a precipitant and identifies a reversible target.
interpretation.negative_finding: No high-risk or recently changed drugs. Does not exclude delirium; shifts attention to infection, metabolic, withdrawal and structural causes.
interpretation.pitfalls: Delirium is usually multifactorial, so a culprit drug does not end the search. Abrupt stopping of benzodiazepines or opioids can itself precipitate delirium or withdrawal.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: hold or taper the offending drug(s) and reassess; negative: keep looking for infectious, metabolic, withdrawal or CNS causes.

sources.citation: Inouye SK, Charpentier PA. Precipitating factors for delirium in hospitalized elderly persons. Predictive model and interrelationship with baseline vulnerability. JAMA 1996;275:852-857.
Clegg A, Young JB. Which medications to avoid in people at risk of delirium: a systematic review. Age Ageing 2011;40:23-29.
Tune L, Carr S, Cooper T, Klug B, Golinger RC. Association of anticholinergic activity of prescribed medications with postoperative delirium. J Neuropsychiatry Clin Neurosci 1993;5:208-210.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Not a stand-alone diagnostic test; never use a clean medication list to withhold sepsis, metabolic or CNS work-up in an acutely confused patient.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Focal deficits, fever with meningism, or a fall on anticoagulation need imaging/LP pathways regardless of drug list.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Completeness of the drug history depends on the historian and record access; anticholinergic burden scales differ between raters.

extraction_notes: No diagnostic-accuracy study (sens/spec/LR) exists for 'medication review' as an index test for delirium cause. Evidence is risk-association: Inouye 1996 abstract reports adjusted RR 2.9 (95% CI 1.6-5.4) for >3 medications added; Clegg 2011 abstract reports OR 2.5 (1.2-5.2) opioids, 3.0 (1.3-6.8) benzodiazepines, 2.4 (1.0-5.8) dihydropyridines. These are not LRs, so estimates left empty. All PMIDs confirmed via tools/pubmed.py fetch.
